title: Interlock cadence automation and latency window allocator
creator: Aisha Kapoor
acceptance_criteria: Automated interlock calendar populates per-team blocking windows in the roadmap view
Latency window allocator computes dynamic buffer (ms) per release based on historical rollout delays and capacity variance
Slack alerts trigger 72/48/24/4 hours before a blocking handoff with context and suggested mitigations
Dashboard shows predicted contention risk (low/medium/high) for each release lane and allows one-click reassignment
Rollout gate policy prevents final release flag unless guardrails are acknowledged by all dependent teams
comments: 2025-01-12 - Aisha K created ticket after Q1 roadmap sync; observed repeated handoff delays between Serving Runtime and Console teams in Dec/Jan.

2025-01-16 - Kickoff meeting notes: aligned on calculation inputs (historical handoff latency, capacity variance, frequency of hotfixes). Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RD/Interlock+Allocator

2025-01-21 - Eng (Ethan) proposed simple exponential smoothing for buffer calc; Design (Maya) requested UI mocks for per-release swimlane alerts. Action: ENG to prototype algorithm (ENG-9382), DES to produce mocks (DES-2047).

2025-01-28 - Prototype algorithm initial run against last 6 months backlog shows 18% reduction in unexpected cutover delays in simulation. Shared internal Jupyter: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/drive-sim-results
2025-02-03 - Security review triage: SEC requested threat model for automated alerts to avoid leaking internal escalation channels; asked to redact internal owner emails in Slack payloads (SEC-110).

2025-02-10 - Design review: accepted compact swimlane with color-coded contention heat; asked for hover state showing root-cause links (PRDs linked). Design PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/designs/pull/89

2025-02-14 - Engineering update: MVP implementation of allocator merged to staging branch. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/roadmap/pull/412. Observability dashboard draft: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/roadmap/allocator

2025-02-18 - PM review: small but important trade-off documented - aggressive buffer reduces rework but increases perceived schedule slippage. Decision: expose buffer tuning slider per-initiative with default computed by allocator.
2025-02-20 - Blocker noted: Infra (INF-5023) needs additional feature flags for controlled Slack routing; opened dependency with Infra to support canary routing.
decision_log: Use exponential smoothing plus headroom multiplier as default buffer calculation (agreed 2025-01-21).
Expose buffer tuning per-initiative in Console rather than forcing a single org-level value (agreed 2025-02-18).
Send minimal Slack payloads with link to Console details to satisfy SEC review (agreed 2025-02-03).
next_steps: INF-5023: Infra to add canary routing flags (due 2025-02-25).
ENG-9382: finalize allocator config UI and edge-case testing (due 2025-02-28).
DES-2047: finalize hover-state mocks and accessibility review (due 2025-02-27).
PM: schedule pilot with 2 initiatives for March window and collect rollback/adjustment telemetry.
